status: read-only minimal CFEL candidate; no Draft, parser, runtime, or Current source changed
scope: Fenced blocks only; indented code blocks are outside this rule by explicit user decision.

new_selector.name: FENCED_LABELS
exact_rule_text: FENCED_LABELS(p) selects one parsed fence label for every fenced code-block occurrence in the complete recursive Markdown parse of the one scalar Markdown value denoted by p. Duplicate labels remain separate selected values.
Selection uses Markdown block boundaries from that parse, never a regular-expression match. It does not select indented code blocks, create Graph Nodes, or create dependent Properties.
p must resolve to exactly one Markdown scalar. Missing, multi-valued, incomplete, or unavailable Markdown parsing is an evaluation error; it is not an empty selection.

FENCED_LABELS(p){:n} uses the existing allowed-count notation for the selected fence labels. `FENCED_LABELS(p): L` uses the existing allowed-value notation: every selected label must be one of the stated literal labels. The allowed-value test over no selected labels passes vacuously.

For `: CFEL`, CFEL is the existing semantic label in the Formal content rule: a fenced block labelled CFEL carries formal content. This selector does not define whether a raw Markdown info string is whole-string or token parsed. The Markdown-format implementation must bind its parsed fence label to that existing CFEL-labelled-fence meaning before evaluation.
new_selector.minimality: One reusable parsed-Markdown selector only. It reuses existing count and allowed-value syntax; no COUNT, ALL, INFO_STRING, indented-block selector, block graph, or Claim-specific predicate is introduced.

preserved: At most one CFEL fenced block is present.
Other fenced blocks are not allowed in Claim.
Claim remains one required markdown scalar with no child Properties.
constraint_trace.proof: A non-CFEL fence fails `: CFEL`; two CFEL fences fail `{:0..1}`; zero fences pass; the required scalar and zero-child contract remain the first two expressions.

governing_label_evidence.text: A fenced block labelled CFEL carries formal content inside Claim.
governing_label_evidence.handling: The candidate preserves that semantic label. It deliberately does not add a whole-info-string, first-token, case-folding, or metadata policy.

examples.input: ordinary Markdown prose with no fenced code block
one parsed fenced block whose label is CFEL
examples.result: pass; its body is validated separately as CFEL syntax

examples.input: two parsed fenced blocks both labelled CFEL
examples.result: fail; duplicates are retained and count is 2

examples.input: one parsed fenced block labelled yaml
examples.result: fail; yaml is not an allowed label

examples.input: one parsed fenced block with a resolved empty label
examples.result: fail; an empty fence label is not CFEL

examples.input: one four-space-indented code block and no fenced block
examples.result: pass under the explicitly fence-only restriction

examples.input: Markdown scalar whose complete block parse is unavailable
examples.result: evaluation error, not an empty-label pass

application_guard: This Claim has a required single markdown scalar. A future optional markdown Property must guard its occurrence before calling FENCED_LABELS; the selector does not treat absence as an empty value.
implementation_gate: Before evaluation, bind parsed Markdown fence labels to the existing CFEL-labelled-fence meaning. This is a binding gate, not a new semantic rule about raw info-string encoding.
